text: Where does address 0x1000 live? In a direct-mapped cache: in exactly one line.
This is our CSA222 project: a Direct-Mapped Cache Controller in Verilog.
I'm Tathagat Harsh, and with me are M S Thejas, Garv Verma, Parv Goyal and Vaibhav Rajput.
A cache is a small, fast SRAM between the CPU and slow DRAM. It works because programs have locality.
Our cache is 1 KB with 16-byte blocks, so it has 64 lines.
A 32-bit address splits into a 22-bit tag, a 6-bit index and a 4-bit offset.
Direct-mapped means each block has exactly one possible line, chosen by the index. Same index means a fight.
My tag comparator gives: hit = valid AND stored tag equals request tag.
If the valid bit is 0, it's a miss, even when the tags match.
The cache stores everything in three arrays: valid bits, tags and data.
Valid bits are flip-flops: one reset clears all 64, so a garbage tag never gives a false hit.
On a miss the data RAM takes a whole 16-byte block in one cycle. On a write hit, just one word.
Direct-mapped gives the fastest hit path: one compare, no replacement policy. The cost is conflict misses.
I designed the controller: a four-state finite state machine.
IDLE latches the request. COMPARE checks the tag. A read miss goes to ALLOCATE and waits ten cycles for memory.
A read hit finishes in a single cycle.
Every write goes to WRITE_MEM: write-through, no-write-allocate. Memory is always up to date, so no dirty bits.
The hit and miss counters live here, so the hardware measures its own hit rate.
My main-memory model has a ten-cycle latency and returns a whole 128-bit block in one transfer.
dm_cache.v connects six modules into one cache, with main memory outside it.
One command compiles and runs the full testbench.
In the waveform the first read misses and takes 12 cycles. The next three reads hit in one cycle each.
My testbench checks all 2,187 accesses against a golden reference model. Zero errors.
Sequential: 75%, one miss per 4-word block. Repeated: 93.75%, temporal locality. Random: about 10%.
Conflict: 0%. Two addresses 1 KB apart share line 0 and keep evicting each other.
Measured AMAT matches 1 + miss rate × 11 on every single trace.
In Phase II we'll synthesize on Vivado and compare against a 2-way LRU cache.
Thank you!
